paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: sorrow isn't the enemy. Paul says there are two kinds. "Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation without regret, but worldly sorrow brings death." (2 Corinthians 7:10) Same tears, friend, but they do NOT end up at the same address.

Look at the difference. Worldly sorrow just sits in the dark and replays the mess. Godly sorrow turns around and moves, and Paul says it produced "what earnestness, what eagerness to clear yourselves" (2 Corinthians 7:11). That's a sorrow with a destination. Paul even admits he regretted sending that hard letter for a while, but it led them to repentance (2 Corinthians 7:8-9), and I think that tells you something about how kind a hard truth can be.

So when you feel that sting of getting something wrong, baker, don't hide from it. Let it point you back to God and to the people you love, because He is the One "who comforts the downcast" (2 Corinthians 7:6). I've been stuck in the dark with my own sorrow, and I promise you the sting was never the end of the story. Let it lead you somewhere, and you'll end up with joy that overflows, just like Paul's.
